# PCB comparisons with real Altium

The PCB corpus contains **46 existing snapshots** (35 real-board views and 11
synthetic cases). `coverage.json` lists every one, including its source hash and
capture status. A test checks that this inventory matches the PCB snapshots on
disk, so an omitted case cannot disappear silently.

**27 snapshots currently have real references.** Their existing snapshot files
are replaced with side-by-side comparisons: real Altium on the left, and the
exact SVG generated by the original test on the right. The earlier two extra
`*-altium-comparison.snap.svg` files are removed. Existing geometry assertions,
source PCB documents, and board viewports are retained.

The other 19 snapshots retain their original output while their capture blockers
are addressed. They are explicitly listed as `awaiting-reference`; there are no
fabricated images, blank comparison panels, or AltiumTS images labeled as Altium.

## Captured views

| Board | Views |
| --- | --- |
| C17 | Full PCB, top solder mask |
| DSP5509 CIII | Full design including off-board components |
| Elk Pi | Full PCB, top copper, top overlay, bottom routing, inner pad stack, polygon cutout, roundrect pads, slotted pads, rotated pads |
| Novena eDP | Full PCB, mechanical component bodies, U10C, AUX net, top paste detail, top solder detail |
| AM62L | Top copper, text objects hidden |
| STM32 ST-Link V2 | Full PCB, mechanical layer 7 (named Dimensions in Altium) |
| TI power boards | PMP22650, PMP22712, PMP22773, PMP23595, PMP23653 main and planar transformer |

| `pmp22773.png` | Screenshot 2026-10-02 at 15.42.31.png | 1034 × 1188 | `48ee04bc03187e103e503ec56de8856c43c923ccaef0a2b2911b869aacb1cfc2` |

The remaining images were captured on 2026-10-08 in the official
[Altium 365 Viewer](https://www.altium.com/viewer/) using the exact PCB documents
consumed by the existing tests. They are unchanged browser screenshot bytes,
not another converter's output. Each `<snapshot-name>.json` records the image,
actual MIME type and dimensions, source-document hash, screenshot hash, layer
selection, and crop. The image bytes are embedded in the SVG for offline viewing.
Tests verify their hashes, dimensions, format, and exact embedded bytes.

## TI project strings

The six TI power-board tests also load the matching original `.PrjPcb` from the
same pinned design ZIP as the PCB. The right panel resolves project parameters
such as `PRJ_Number` and `PCB_Rev`; the left panel retains its original reference
pixels. PMP22712 and PMP22773 show the project-aware real Altium screenshots.
Some standalone Altium 365 captures (including PMP23595 and PMP23653 main) show
raw expressions because the project was not loaded in those reference captures.
That input-context difference is intentional and must not be read as an expected
unresolved title. Font sizes and board viewports are retained. Modern native text
with an explicitly disabled justification flag uses its saved origin with
lower-left alignment, before applying rotation and mirroring. Active alignment
and older records without that flag keep their existing behavior.

## Crop and layer alignment

The converter panel retains its original dimensions and aspect ratio. The
reference viewport maps the same board-space area into the real screenshot.
Full-board views include the original test's padding; detail views use its
configured board-unit `viewBox`. Captures use the matching single layer when the
test specifies one. Default views intentionally preserve the real viewer's
presentation, including differences in visible layers and colors.

For the new captures, alignment uses the real viewer's visible SVG overlay
transform and iframe bounds. C17/DSP and the uploaded PNGs use measured board
outline bounds. Raw image files remain intact; SVG clipping removes browser
controls outside the canvas. Gray padding is added only beyond the captured
canvas. A capture's world-space view and transform are recorded in its JSON.

Altium's component/net selection dims unrelated primitives rather than removing
them. The U10C and AUX reference captures retain that native selection behavior;
the AltiumTS side keeps its original component/net filters. Small detail crops
remain limited by the captured raster resolution. These are visual baselines,
not pixel-equality or font-metric measurements.

## Elk Pi baseline verification

The comparison panels were checked against a separate copy of the PR base
commit, `4cf4aad7357c733b72dd85f97fdfeab70e4ba502`, using the same fixture and
the original tests' layer, title, and `viewBox` options. Both panels embed the
base renderer's output **byte for byte**. Production rendering has not changed.

The old checked-in SVG markup differs from a fresh base render in two cases:

- Bottom routing still contains all **42 pads, including all 20 MULTILAYER
  pads**. Its complete SVG-line multiset is unchanged; the apparent pad deletions
  are moves caused by the renderer's existing paint order. The test now checks
  both pad counts in addition to the visual snapshot.
- The middle-layer view gains one `MID1` polygon outline with `fill="none"`
  and the standard `xmlns:xlink` namespace. The outline is already emitted by
  the base renderer; its edges are outside the 120-by-120 crop. The existing
  board outline, region, and pad are unchanged.

Rasterizing each old golden and fresh base output at its original size produces
**zero changed pixel channels** for both cases. `bun-match-svg` compares rendered
pixels and retains an existing golden when pixels match, even during snapshot
updates. That left the older element order/off-crop markup in these two goldens;
creating comparison snapshots exposed the already-existing renderer output.

For reproducing the check, the Elk Pi source SHA-256 is
`8d61c6c9b9eff6748340794db203a86057857b8ce0348b7510859d73e3bce210`.
The fresh standalone base-render SVG hashes (before comparison wrapping) are:

| View | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| Bottom routing | `dc9a9d430eb18445d17da73a41909367a89d14949e6e2fbcfbde6e323acf2cac` |
| Middle-layer pad stack | `a19ba8b8991b7fe0f1d29bff1cc5066d4686776c15a1abe4852534f0c7dc4a88` |

## Remaining captures

The exact cases and reasons are in `coverage.json`:

- CH582, Sample Board, SimpleFOC Shield, and SimpleFOC Mini use ASCII PcbDocs.
  Altium 365 rejected the original files in single-design ZIPs (Mini was also
  tried directly). Safe native serialization cannot preserve all their records.
- Synthetic fixtures need native Altium reference captures. The generated binary
  fixtures tested in the viewer did not yield usable renders; some remained at
  `Processing the Design`, and the component-body upload returned to the home
  view. The region and keepout-arc fixtures also cannot be serialized safely by
  the current binary writer. Their existing repros are preserved.

AM62L was successfully captured after uploading a compressed single-board ZIP.
Its original SVG test still stalled in a bounded 120-second run. The comparison
was assembled around the existing golden SVG; its right panel was not regenerated
or validated by a completed renderer run. The test is wired to generate the same
comparison when that existing stall is fixed.

Completing these cases requires Altium to open the exact fixtures and produce
reference screenshots. Do not strip unsupported fields, change geometry, or
substitute a different board just to obtain a reference.

## Regeneration

```sh
bun run download-references
BUN_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 bun test tests/svg
bun test tests/altium-reference-comparison.test.ts
```

The known AM62L stall may prevent a complete SVG run. Normal tests compare the
existing snapshot filenames; future rendering fixes update the right panel
while retaining the reference bytes. When a pending reference becomes
available, add its image/JSON, wrap that test's existing SVG using
`renderAltiumReferenceComparison`, and mark the case captured in `coverage.json`.
